title: model-loading-weights-shard-breadcrumbs-evan-murphy
summary: Scratchpad notes for recurring model load failures tied to weights shard downloads and checkpoint format mismatches (observations, commands tried, hypotheses, next steps).
body:
Top-level problem:
Observed intermittent model load failures during startup when loading weights shards from S3-backed artifact store. Failures show up as corrupted shard reads or unexpected EOFs and sometimes as format mismatch errors (safetensors vs torch). Happened 2026-02-11 through 2026-02-12 on canary and a single Dedicated node.\n\nTimeline / symptoms:
- 2026-02-11 09:22: attempted canary deploy, runtime failed to finish warmup (stuck at model init).\n- Logs: multiple shards reported as size 0 or truncated, worker printed "Unexpected EOF while reading object" for torch.load path.\n- 2026-02-12 02:17 observed one node successfully load the model but later in runtime traces saw partial KV cache population for some tokens (suggests partial shard).\n\nCommands & things tried (raw):
- aws s3 ls s3://redwood-model-artifacts/prod/model-v2/ --recursive --human-readable | grep weights
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-model-artifacts/prod/model-v2/weights-00001-of-00008.pt ./weights-00001-of-00008.pt
- curl -I https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood-model-artifacts/prod/model-v2/weights-00001-of-00008.pt
- range test: curl -r 0-1023 -sSf -o /tmp/head.bin https://.../weights-00001-of-00008.pt && hexdump -C /tmp/head.bin | head
- md5sum checks: aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-model-artifacts --key prod/model-v2/weights-00001-of-00008.pt --query ETag
- python quick loader: 
  import torch
  torch.load('weights-00001-of-00008.pt', map_location='cpu')
  --> RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading an object
- tried safetensors loader for shards that are labeled .safetensors: 
  from safetensors import safe_open
  safe_open('weights-00003-of-00008.safetensors', framework='pt')
  --> safetensors.errors.SafetyError: invalid header (offset=0)
\nObserved outputs & logs (snippets):
- serving-runtime log (canary-3):
  [2026-02-11T09:22:07Z] ERROR load_manager: shard=weights-00001-of-00008.pt status=corrupt read_bytes=0 expected=2147483648
  [2026-02-11T09:22:07Z] ERROR model_init: failed to map shard weights-00001-of-00008.pt -> RuntimeError("unexpected EOF while reading an object")
- s3 access logs (partial):
  2026-02-11T09:21:59Z 200 GET /prod/model-v2/weights-00001-of-00008.pt 206 Range 0-
  2026-02-11T09:22:02Z 200 GET /prod/model-v2/weights-00002-of-00008.pt 206 Range 0-
  2026-02-11T09:22:04Z 408 GET /prod/model-v2/weights-00004-of-00008.pt - connection closed by peer
- curl/responses: intermittent 206 (partial content) vs 200; sometimes connection reset mid-download.\n\nHypotheses (ranked):
1) S3-backed artifact store intermittently returning truncated objects due to multipart upload/replication inconsistency or proxy (edge) bug. Evidence: Range requests returning 206 then subsequent full-get returning truncated file and load error. Also observed connection resets.\n2) Artifact manifest/index points to wrong byte ranges or wrong shard ordering (manifest generation bug). Evidence: one shard seemed to be 0 bytes according to runtime; but head-object shows non-zero size in S3 occasionally -> suggests race or manifest stale.\n3) Checkpoint format mismatch (some shards in safetensors, some in torch .pt) and loader selection code sometimes picks wrong loader based on file extension or metadata. Evidence: safetensors loader failing with invalid header for files with .safetensors extension (maybe renamed).\n4) Runtime parallel downloader bug that corrupts file if multiple workers write same temp file (race). Evidence: temp file names use pid but not unique enough across containers? need to verify.\n\nRepro steps attempted (notes):
- Manual download of the same shard from my laptop: repeated 10x, 2/10 returned truncated file (md5 mismatch). Tried different regions (us-west-2, us-east-1) via GET URL -> still flaky but less frequent.\n- curl with --retry 5 and --fail improved success rate, but still saw 1/20 failures.\n- Reconstructed by reuploading a known-good shard from build artifacts to a test bucket -> loads consistently. So issue seems tied to prod bucket or the way uploads were performed (maybe multipart).\n\nImmediate mitigations tried in cluster: 
- Added aggressive retry and integrity check (etag compare) in load manager: if MD5/ETag mismatch, re-fetch. Reduced incident surface but did not eliminate since some truncated reads still matched a broken ETag (possible multipart etag behavior).\n- Force use of full-range GET rather than range-chunks in downloader to avoid partial edge caching. Increased startup time but reduced errors in canary.\n\nNotes on ETag and multipart uploads:
- ETag for multipart uploads is not simple MD5, so using it to validate single-part integrity is invalid. Need to record manifest-level checksum (sha256) at upload time.\n\nOpen questions / next steps:
- Can we get S3 server-side logs for the failing GETs? Talk to infra (storage team) to check for proxy/edge errors 408/connection resets around 2026-02-11T09:21:50-09:22:10.\n- Re-run reproducer from a Dedicated machine in same VPC to isolate network/proxy. (Priya to run).\n- Add deterministic artifact manifest that includes per-shard sha256 (CI to compute & attach), and change load path to validate sha256 after download.\n- Harden downloader to write to unique temp files + atomic rename to avoid cross-worker races.\n- Add telemetry on content-length vs bytes-read and emit an alert if mismatch > 0.\n\nQuick action items (who):
- Evan: create a small test that repeatedly fetches shards via the same node pool to estimate failure rate (in progress).
- Priya: ask infra/storage for S3/edge logs and confirm if there were any networking incidents in that window.
- Jordan: review downloader temp file naming & atomic write path in serving-runtime (PR suggested: linked PR).
- Ops: consider re-uploading prod model-v2 artifacts with single-part uploads or precomputed sha256 manifest if we confirm multipart artifacts correlate with failures.\n\nRelated tickets / pointers:
- INF-3421 (investigation) - linked above
- PR: serving-runtime#1284 (temp file uniqueness + retries) - draft
- Confluence: artifact-ingest-checksums (proposal to add sha256 to manifest)\n\nRandom notes / ramblings (scratch):
- Could be exacerbated by node autoscaler creating a lot of concurrent downloads around deploy time -> saturates egress and leads to truncated reads. Check how many parallel fetches we spawn during model warmup (default 8 per model). Consider staggered fetch or caching layer.
- If we adopt on-disk shard caching across pods, we can avoid re-download storms during rolling restarts. Need eviction policy.\n\nSummary: Evidence points to flaky downloads from prod artifact store (likely multipart/edge/proxy issue) combined with weak integrity checking in loader. Short-term patch: stronger retries + full-get + atomic writes. Medium: sha256 manifests + loader validation + CI to enforce single-format uploads. Long-term: distributed download cache / CDN or pre-pulled images to avoid runtime storms.\n\nWill update after infra log response and after Jordan's PR review.\n
